storyTemplate.title: The Unwanted Inheritance
storyTemplate.description: After inheriting a grandparent's rural house, the player tries to build an ordinary small-town life while locked doors, familiar objects, and a false urn begin exposing a family horror below the floor.

story_source.title: The Unwanted Inheritance
story_source.description: Original general-audience horror story about an inherited family house, a dead twin's grudge spirit, and the lie hidden beneath the cellar.

player.name: Caleb Ward
player.role: new heir to the grandparents' old house
player.personality_description: A practical adult trying to turn an inherited family house into a livable start. They remember the house fondly from childhood visits, but their choices, courage, denial, anger, and curiosity are decided through play.
player.speech_style: Natural and grounded, with tone shaped by the player's choices.
starting_known_facts: This is one of three selectable player characters for the story.
They inherited their grandparents' old rural house after probate finished.
They accepted a job at a local hardware store and plan to live in the house while deciding whether to keep or sell it.
They remember visiting the house as a child and having warm daytime memories there.
They remember having a twin who died young and was supposedly cremated; the twin's urn sits on the fireplace.
Caleb's twin brother was named Noah.

full_character.name: Celia Brandt
full_character.personality_description: A brisk small-town lawyer who has seen families become strange around inherited property. She is not cruel, but she has learned not to volunteer what clients did not ask.
starting_known_facts: Celia Brandt handled the transfer of the grandparents' house to the player.
She knows the estate paperwork but does not know the full cellar truth.
She can answer questions about the will, property records, insurance requirements, and legal deadlines.
She remembers that several relatives refused or ignored the inheritance before it passed to the player.
She avoids family gossip unless pushed with evidence.

full_character.name: Deacon Miles
full_character.personality_description: A steady local business owner who gives practical advice and notices when customers buy the wrong things for the wrong reasons.
full_character.speech_style: Plainspoken, dry, and helpful until a question sounds dangerous.
starting_known_facts: Deacon Miles owns Grayling Hardware and hired the player for steady work.
He knew the grandparents as careful customers who bought locks, chain, salt, batteries, and repair supplies with strange regularity.
He gives the player a normal daytime anchor outside the house.
He can provide tools, gossip, and warnings without understanding the full haunting.
He is more useful when the player asks concrete questions instead of sounding panicked.

full_character.name: June Harlan
full_character.personality_description: A lonely neighbor who remembers too much and has spent years deciding which silences were kindness and which were cowardice.
full_character.speech_style: Soft, evasive, and full of unfinished sentences.
starting_known_facts: June Harlan lives across the road from the inherited house.
She remembers the player visiting as a child but never staying overnight.
She remembers the night the twin died, though not every detail.
She knows the grandparents changed after the death and bought heavy locks soon after.
She may tell the truth if the player brings enough evidence or if the house pressure becomes impossible to ignore.

world_flags.tone: grounded supernatural horror with small-town normal life at daytime and escalating family horror at night
world_flags.horror_control: The narrator may impose fear, dread, sensory distortion, intrusive memories, hesitation, nightmares, lost time, and unreliable perception when the haunting escalates, but must not decide the player's major moral choices.

story_rules.text: This is a horror story. The narrator may impose fear responses, sensory distortions, intrusive memories, hesitation, panic, dread, nightmares, lost time, compulsive attention, and unreliable perception when the house or twin spirit pressure escalates. The narrator must not decide major moral choices for the player, but may make the player frightened, physically affected, misled by perception, or temporarily overwhelmed when the horror justifies it.
The active supernatural entity is the dead twin's grudge spirit, not the old bargaining force. The twin spirit is angry, lonely, betrayed, and fixated on the surviving sibling.
The player starts knowing only the family story: the twin died young and was cremated. The truth about the grandparents' bargain, the false urn, and the cellar burial must emerge through play.

world_notes: The player inherited the grandparents' old house and has started a small-town job at Grayling Hardware.
The player has fond childhood memories of daytime visits to the house but never slept there before.
The twin's urn sits on the fireplace and is familiar to the player as part of the family story.
unresolved_threads: Why did the grandparents never let the player sleep in the house?
What is really inside the urn?
Did the player's parents know the grandparents lied?
What is behind the locked cellar door?
rules_and_constraints: Keep the horror concrete and clue-driven rather than abstract.
Daytime scenes should support normal life, work, errands, local conversations, and house sorting.
Night scenes may become more forceful and frightening as house_pressure rises.

messages.speaker: Narrator
messages.text:
The key sticks the first time you turn it.

Your grandparents' old house opens with a tired wooden groan and the smell of dust, old curtains, and summer visits you remember better than you expected.

Boxes wait in the hall. The estate folder is under your arm. Your first shift at Grayling Hardware starts tomorrow morning.

For now, the house is quiet.
